content.value_statement: Refactoring can break behavior when tests and measurements are weak. This skill guides incremental TDD refactoring with test baselines, code smell checks, and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides pre-refactor test baselines and full-suite verification.
Lists common code smells and matching refactoring techniques.
Recommends SOLID principles and design patterns for cleaner structure.
Prompts incremental changes with rollback planning when tests fail.
Provides a TypeScript extract-method example for refactoring flow.
limitations: Does not include runnable scripts or automated test execution.
Requires the agent to know the project test commands and architecture.
Does not guarantee better performance without project-specific measurements.
References resources/implementation-playbook.md, but that file is not included.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Modules
use_cases.description: Plan small behavior-preserving changes before changing risky legacy code.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safer Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use test baselines, code smell checks, and final verification before review.

use_cases.title: Teach Refactor Discipline
use_cases.description: Show teams how to separate behavior changes from structure improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module and create a TDD refactor plan. Identify tests to run, safe first steps, and expected verification.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Small Refactors
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the TDD refactor phase to this code. Keep behavior unchanged, make small changes, and report test results after each step.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Design Debt
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this service for code smells, SOLID issues, and performance risks. Propose measured refactors with rollback checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Large Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a large legacy refactor using branch-by-abstraction or Mikado planning. Map dependencies, verify coverage, and separate behavior changes.

output_examples.input: Refactor a long order processing method with passing tests.
output_examples.output: A test baseline, an extract-method plan, applied refactor steps, final green test status, and remaining technical debt notes.

output_examples.input: Improve a slow service without changing behavior.
output_examples.output: A measurement-first plan, likely bottlenecks, proposed data structure changes, regression checks, and before-and-after performance notes.

output_examples.input: Prepare a risky module for a safer pull request.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering coverage gaps, incremental commits, rollback points, documentation updates, and final reviewer summary.

best_practices: Start with a green test baseline before changing structure.
Make one small refactor at a time and verify after each change.
Measure performance before optimizing algorithms, queries, or caching.
anti_patterns: Mixing new behavior with refactoring in the same change.
Applying design patterns without a clear maintainability benefit.
Continuing after a failing test without isolating the breaking change.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents refactor code through a TDD process while preserving existing behavior.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to run relevant tests using the project commands.

faq.question: Can it choose design patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests patterns only when they improve clarity, boundaries, or maintainability.

faq.question: Is it useful for performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends measuring before and after any optimization.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the target code, test command, current failures, and refactoring goal.
